solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Overwhelmed as a peat-cutter?

definitions.meaning: swamped by too much work or trouble
peat is dug from a bog, so a peat-cutter is literally stuck down in the bog

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone swamped by work feels like a labourer cutting peat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: someone digging peat is down in a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuck in mud is the idiom for being swamped and unable to make progress.

clue.text: Ram's bottom

definitions.meaning: to strike head-first, as a goat or ram does
the rump or backside, an informal word for it

explanation.surface: Reads as a description of a male sheep's rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ram' looks like the animal but is the verb, and the 's stands for 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for striking with the head and an informal noun for the buttocks.

clue.text: Disappear, as may one man and his dog?

definitions.meaning: to go missing, as an object that vanishes

definitions.text: as may one man and his dog?
definitions.meaning: a man taking his dog out for exercise sets off on a stroll, the British phrase used to a pet

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a man and his dog might vanish together, echoing the old BBC sheepdog show 'One Man and His Dog'.
explanation.walkthrough: The British slang phrase means to go missing, especially of an object; literally it is what dog-walkers do.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal idiom: something that has been stolen or lost is said to have taken itself off for a stroll.

clue.text: Legal term a lot easier, initially, when written up

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the letters are read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: pots of money means a lot

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word easier

explanation.surface: Suggests some legal jargon becomes easier to grasp once written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when written up' reverses POTS + E into ESTOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Estoppel law uses this verb: to bar a party from asserting something contrary to an earlier position.

clue.text: Three musical neighbours let down

parts.note: three adjacent notes in the chromatic scale: D, then E flat, then E, written out in full
three adjacent notes in the chromatic scale: D, then E flat, then E, written out in full
three adjacent notes in the chromatic scale: D, then E flat, then E, written out in full

explanation.surface: Three musicians living next door are disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: On a keyboard D, E flat and E are side-by-side keys, so the three neighbours are written D, EFLAT, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflate a tyre or balloon is to let the air out of it, i.e. let it down.

clue.text: Beast with a growth that's deformed

indicators.note: deformed means put out of shape, so the letters of the phrase a growth are rearranged

explanation.surface: Describes an animal disfigured by a lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's deformed' rearranges A GROWTH; the surface is apt since the animal is named for the wart-like lumps on its face.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild African pig is an example of a beast, an animal.

clue.text: Among autocrats, a real despot

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the run of words autocrats, a real

explanation.surface: Picks out one true tyrant from a group of autocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among' signals the letters lying inside autocraTS A Real.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor wielded absolute power, so the title stands for any despot.

clue.text: Change dress

explanation.surface: An instruction to put on different clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like a verb paired with 'Change' but is a noun: a loose straight garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for altering or moving and a noun for a loose straight frock.

clue.text: Privileged individual with plenty of money in hand

parts.note: a member of a royal family is a privileged person
flush means having plenty of cash

explanation.surface: A rich, privileged person holds the money in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hand' points to cards: the top poker holding.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, ace-to-ten in one suit is the highest possible holding of cards, a hand.

clue.text: One going about ornamental garden

parts.note: one who departs is a parter
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone strolling round a formal garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One going' is a made-up agent noun: someone who parts company.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal flat garden of patterned beds, typical of French chateaux, is an ornamental garden.

clue.text: That is what to do with a broken-down car!

definitions.text: what to do with a broken-down car!
definitions.meaning: a breakdown truck must haul the car away

explanation.surface: Gives advice on dealing with a car that has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase meaning 'namely' also reads literally as an instruction to haul the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal phrase meaning namely, used like 'i.e.' to introduce an example.

clue.text: Figure touring country observed ceremony

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the number wraps round the country

parts.note: a figure here is a number, forty
Mali is a West African country

explanation.surface: A person travelling through a country watched a ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' means a number here, not a shape or a person; 'touring' signals going round.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure done for form's sake, a ritual carried out because convention requires it.

clue.text: Strike, a bit careless

parts.note: to slap is to strike with the open hand
a dash of something is a small amount

explanation.surface: Hitting someone is rather thoughtless.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: work done hastily and without care is slipshod.

clue.text: Wreck is gross

definitions.meaning: to destroy completely, as a car in a crash

explanation.surface: Declares that a wrecked object is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' looks like 'disgusting' but means the whole sum.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for writing off a car and an adjective or noun for an entire sum.

clue.text: E, my love?

parts.note: the letter E is the centre letter of the word sweet, i.e. its heart

explanation.surface: Seems a lover's note: an initial, then an endearment.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards from the answer: the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a lover, like 'darling' or 'dear'.

clue.text: Is it right defined by 'squirm'?

indicators.note: defined by means bounded or enclosed by, so the letter for right sits within the synonym for squirm

parts.note: to wiggle is to squirm

explanation.surface: A pedant asks whether a word is properly defined by squirm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defined by' means bounded by: R sits inside WIGGLE. The whole clue also serves as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe or twist the body about is to squirm.

clue.text: Welcome case of golfer teeing off

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters
off means wrong or faulty, so the letters of teeing are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer is hailed as they tee off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes GR from golfer; 'off' rearranges TEEING to EETING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a salutation offered on arrival is a welcome.

clue.text: Lass pressing a very yellow flower

indicators.note: pressing means holding tight in the middle, so the girl's letters hold the others

parts.note: a lass is a girl
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A girl presses a bright yellow flower, as in a scrapbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' looks like flower-pressing but means squeezing round: the lass holds the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the sunflower, whose head turns to follow the sun.

clue.text: Left among rotten fish, feel for the time when still fresh

indicators.note: among says the letter goes in the middle of the rearranged letters
rotten means decayed or bad, so the letters of fish and feel are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone checks how long fish stays fresh by feeling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' rearranges FISH FEEL; 'among' sets L within the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The period a product can be stored and sold before it goes off.

clue.text: 'Chinese', for example, has 'E' at the back

parts.note: the letter as given
astern means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Points out that the word Chinese ends in E.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface spots the E at the end of 'Chinese'; really E is placed before a nautical word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese culture is an example of something Oriental, from the Far East.

clue.text: Talk about one getting smarter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for talk goes round the numeral

parts.note: to natter is to chat or talk
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Talk of someone becoming more elegant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside NATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning neat and smartly dressed.

clue.text: Is 'in the past' defining 'present', on the other hand?

indicators.note: defining means marking the limits of, so the past tense surrounds the word for present

parts.note: the past tense of is gives was
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A grammarian's puzzle about tenses defining one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defining' means marking the edges; 'present' is not a tense here but means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjunction introducing a contrast, meaning 'while by contrast'.

clue.text: Appealing in some cases, lose then?

explanation.surface: Wonders whether an appeal will sometimes fail.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'you win some, you lose some' is split: the second half is in the clue, the first half is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A charming, engaging manner is attractive, i.e. appealing.

clue.text: Native American tribe heading for Texas get lost!

parts.note: the Hopi are a Native American people of Arizona

indicators.note: heading for points to the opening letter of the word Texas

explanation.surface: A tribe heads for Texas and is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like travel but takes T from Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang command telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Welcoming bald finale, shave father

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the word for shave holds the letter

parts.note: to pare is to shave or trim

indicators.note: the finale is the end, so the closing letter of the word bald

explanation.surface: A barber invites a balding priest for a final shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welcoming' puts D (end of 'bald') inside PARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A military chaplain or priest is addressed as Father.

clue.text: Island where last of luggage, sack and bag sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the assembled letters are read in reverse order
last of points to the closing letter of the word luggage

parts.note: to fire is to sack an employee
to net is to catch or bag

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker's luggage goes astray and is sent back from the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses E + FIRE + NET.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the Canary Islands, a Spanish holiday island.

clue.text: Zealous command subordinate to god

indicators.note: subordinate to means placed below, so in this down answer the command goes under the god

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
a bid is an order or command, as in to bid someone go

explanation.surface: A fanatic obeys orders from on high.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'subordinate to' puts BID below RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme, fanatical enthusiasm, as of a rabid supporter.

clue.text: County wards have them

definitions.meaning: short for Bedfordshire, an English county
hospital wards contain them for patients

explanation.surface: A county's electoral wards have something.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDS is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, a county north of London; 'wards' are hospital wards, not electoral ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Short form of Bedfordshire, an English county; also what patients lie in.

clue.text: Furthermore, nation reforming at a slowish pace

parts.note: and means furthermore, adding something

indicators.note: reforming means shaping again, so the letters of nation are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sounds like a politician's promise of gradual national reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' rearranges NATION to ANTINO.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking, a little faster or slower than walking pace.

clue.text: Brummie intellect seeking some solution?

indicators.note: someone from Birmingham, whose accent turns the vowel of the word for intellect into an 'eye' sound

parts.note: the brain is the seat of intellect

explanation.surface: A clever Birmingham person looks for an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brummie is a native of Birmingham, England; the local accent famously shifts 'ay' towards 'eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: Salty water is a solution of salt, an example, hence 'some' and the question mark.

clue.text: Sound of collaborative group in swarm

indicators.note: sound of means the word is said aloud and a word matching it in sound is written

parts.note: a team is a group working together

explanation.surface: The noise a team makes when swarming.
explanation.definitionFit: To be full of and swarming with, as a pond with fish.

clue.text: Alone, so the weekend never arrives?

definitions.meaning: if Friday goes on without end, the weekend can never begin

explanation.surface: A lonely person feels the weekend will never come.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as FRI ENDLESS: Friday without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no companions means being solitary, alone.
